perspective:
From Keith’s perspective, he knows/experienced the following:

- Elizabeth is his colleague and the receptionist at the construction company; they have a friendly but professional relationship through his office visits for paperwork/project updates.
- Recently, Elizabeth seemed unusually curt or short with him. He wondered if he had upset her, possibly through a misunderstanding or an unknown mistake.
- He asked her if he had done something wrong. She denied it, said she was dealing with personal stuff, and apologized if she seemed short.
- He felt sympathetic and offered to listen/talk, suggesting a coffee break. She accepted, thanked him, and said it was kind.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her stress; to Keith, it seemed serious. He suggested she consider talking to a professional for an external perspective. She said she had thought about it but was unsure and hesitant about seeking help.
- Afterward, he noticed she became slightly withdrawn. He worried his suggestion may have overstepped or embarrassed her, and he felt regretful.
- He reassured her that he hoped he hadn’t overstepped and that he was there to support her. She said he hadn’t overstepped, appreciated his concern, and said it was a lot to think about.
- Later, Elizabeth seemed more open and appreciative. Keith believed she valued his support and felt more comfortable around him.
- He told her he was glad they talked and that he was always available to chat or take a break. She thanked him, said it meant a lot, and said she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith intends to maintain this supportive relationship with her.
